mappings.Class Definition: An indication that homozygous expression of the SIRPA V2 allele has been detected in a sample.

A genetic finding indicating that a subject expresses the HA-2 genotype, which is defined as either homozygous or heterozygous expression of guanine at position 145 of the MYO1G gene, which encodes valine at amino acid residue 49 MYO1G(V). The MYO1G(V) form of unconventional myosin-Ig protein can be processed into a nonapeptide that can be presented by antigen expressing cells and recognized by HLA-A*0201 (HA-2+), while a variant MYO1G gene with adenine at position 145, which encodes a methionine at amino acid residue 49 (MYO1G(M)) does not produce a peptide that can be displayed by antigen presenting cells (HA-2-).
An indication that simultaneous expression of the wild-type (ALDH2*1) and loss of function (ALDH2*2) alleles of the ADLH2 gene have been detected in a sample.

An assay used to determine which hepatitis B virus genome(s) is present in an infection. Seven genotypes of HBV (designated A through G) have been identified. Different genotypes are prevalent in different geographical areas and each carries a different risk of development of hepatocellular carcinoma.
An assay for determining the genotype(s) of hepatitis C virus (HCV) in plasma or serum from HCV-infected individuals. Six major genotypes are recognized and they vary in their response to treatment.

A genetic finding indicating that both copies of chromosome 16 each have a copy of the hemoglobin beta gene (HBB) with loss of function or gene deletion mutations (B0). This genotype is associated with beta thalassemia major.
Indicates whether the genotypes found in a pair of matched normal and tumor-bearing tissue samples are the same.
mappings.Class Name: Genotype Match Indicator for Normal/Tumor Matched Tissue Samples
mappings.Mapped Term Label: Genotype Match Indicator for Normal/Tumor Matched Tissue Samples

mappings.Class Definition: A genetic finding indicating that neither copy of chromosome 16 has any functional copies of the hemoglobin alpha (HBA) genes. This genotype is associated with hemoglobin Barts.
A genetic finding indicating the genetic composition in a subject for the genes that encode hemoglobin subunits.

A genetic finding indicating the genotype in a subject for the genes that encode hemoglobin subunit alpha, HBA1 and HBA2. Since the two HBA genes encode the same protein and are co-located on chromosome 16, the normal genotype is comprised of 2 maternal alpha genes and 2 paternal alpha genes (aa/aa).

A genetic finding indicating that both copies of chromosome 16 each has two functional copies of the hemoglobin alpha (HBA) genes, which includes 2 maternal alpha genes and 2 paternal alpha genes. This genotype is characterized by normal alpha globin production.

A genetic finding indicating that one copy of chromosome 16 has two functional copies of the hemoglobin alpha (HBA) genes and the other copy of has only one functional HBA gene. This genotype is associated with the alpha thalassemia silent trait.
mappings.Class Name: Hemoglobin Alpha One Copy Deleted Genotype
mappings.Mapped Term Label: Hemoglobin Alpha One Copy Deleted Genotype

mappings.Class Definition: A genetic finding indicating that one copy of chromosome 16 has two functional copies of the hemoglobin alpha (HBA) genes and the other copy of has no functional HBA genes. This genotype is associated with the alpha thalassemia trait.
A genetic finding indicating that both copies of chromosome 16 each have only one functional hemoglobin alpha (HBA) gene. This genotype is associated with the alpha thalassemia trait.

A genetic finding indicating that one copy of chromosome 16 has only one functional copy of a hemoglobin alpha (HBA) gene and the other copy of has no functional HBA genes. This genotype is associated with hemoglobin H disease.
mappings.Class Name: Hemoglobin Alpha Three Copies Deleted Genotype
mappings.Mapped Term Label: Hemoglobin Alpha Three Copies Deleted Genotype

mappings.Class Definition: A genetic finding indicating that one copy of chromosome 16 has one functional copy of a hemoglobin alpha (HBA) gene and one copy that encodes an HBA stop loss mutation called hemoglobin Constant Spring (CS), while the other copy of chromosome 16 has no functional HBA genes. This genotype is associated with a severe form of hemoglobin H disease.
mappings.Class Name: Hemoglobin Alpha cis-Deletion with Constant Spring Genotype
mappings.Mapped Term Label: Hemoglobin Alpha cis-Deletion with Constant Spring Genotype

mappings.Class Definition: A genetic finding indicating that both copies of chromosome 16 each have one functional copy of the hemoglobin beta (HBB) gene. This genotype is characterized by normal beta globin production.

A genetic finding indicating that both copies of chromosome 16 each have a copy of the hemoglobin beta gene (HBB) with mutations that lead to hemoglobin subunit beta insufficiency (B+). This genotype is associated with beta thalassemia intermedia.

A genetic finding indicating that one copy of chromosome 16 has a hemoglobin beta gene (HBB) with mutations that lead to hemoglobin subunit beta insufficiency (B+) and the other copy has HBB loss of function or gene deletion mutations (B0). This genotype is associated with beta thalassemia intermedia.
mappings.Class Name: Hemoglobin Beta Heterozygous Insufficiency Plus Null Genotype
mappings.Mapped Term Label: Hemoglobin Beta Heterozygous Insufficiency Plus Null Genotype

mappings.Class Definition: A genetic finding indicating that one copy of chromosome 16 has a hemoglobin beta gene (HBB) with mutations that lead to hemoglobin subunit beta insufficiency (B+) and the other copy has an HBB mutation that produces a hemoglobin subunit beta variant, the hemoglobin beta E variant, where the glutamic acid residue at position 27 has been replaced by lysine (BE). This genotype is associated with beta thalassemia intermedia.
mappings.Class Name: Hemoglobin Beta Heterozygous Hemoglobin E Plus Insufficiency Genotype
mappings.Mapped Term Label: Hemoglobin Beta Heterozygous Hemoglobin E Plus Insufficiency Genotype

mappings.Class Definition: A genetic finding indicating that one copy of chromosome 16 has a hemoglobin beta gene (HBB) with a mutation that produces a hemoglobin subunit beta variant, the hemoglobin beta E variant, where the glutamic acid residue at position 27 has been replaced by lysine (BE) and the other copy has HBB loss of function or gene deletion mutations (B0). This genotype is associated with beta thalassemia intermedia.
mappings.Class Name: Hemoglobin Beta Heterozygous Hemoglobin E Plus Null Genotype
mappings.Mapped Term Label: Hemoglobin Beta Heterozygous Hemoglobin E Plus Null Genotype

mappings.Class Definition: A genetic finding indicating that one copy of chromosome 16 has a functional copy (B) of the hemoglobin beta gene (HBB) and the other copy has HBB mutations that lead to hemoglobin subunit beta insufficiency (B+). This genotype is associated with beta thalassemia minor.

A genetic finding indicating that one copy of chromosome 16 has a functional copy (B) of the hemoglobin beta gene (HBB) and the other copy has HBB loss of function or gene deletion mutations (B0). This genotype is associated with beta thalassemia minor.
An assay used to determine the genes and molecular markers present in the germline DNA of an individual.
An indication that hepatitis C virus genotype 4 has been detected in a sample.
